Admission: 02.09.2024, 16:05
Ward: UC-2

Referral diagnosis: suspected right femoral neck fracture.

History:
The patient fell at about 09:00 this morning when getting out of bed; the floor was slippery according to her. Severe pain in the right hip, unable to get up. Her daughter raised the alarm and called the GP.

Previous illnesses:
- Arterial hypertension (since about 2014)
- Left distal radius fracture 06/2021
No known allergies. No previous hip surgery.
Smoking: never. Alcohol: occasionally. No other substance use.

Physical examination:
General condition: reduced, severe pain, cooperative. Weight 71 kg, height 163 cm.
Head/neck: normal. Mouth: mucosa moist.
Chest: heart sounds regular, no murmurs. Lungs: vesicular breathing both sides, no crackles.
Abdomen: soft, no tenderness, no masses.

BP 162/88 mmHg, pulse 78/min regular, SpO2 97%, temp 36.8°C.

X-ray pelvis/right hip: medial femoral neck fracture on the right confirmed (Garden III).

Diagnosis:
- Medial femoral neck fracture, right (S72.00)
- Arterial hypertension

- Pain relief: metamizole 1 g IV as needed

P001-D009.title: Surgery report: right total hip replacement
P001-D009.text:
Surgery report
Date: 04.09.2024
Surgeon: Senior Dr Stefan Kralik, trauma surgeon
Assistant: Dr Lukas Bauer
Anaesthesia: spinal anaesthesia (Senior Dr Vera Hochleitner)

Diagnosis: medial femoral neck fracture, right (S72.00)

Indication: right hip fracture, Garden III; surgery indicated after pre-operative information and consent.

Operation: implantation of a cementless total hip replacement, right (manufacturer: ProJoint GmbH, model: PJ-CeraMax, cup 52 mm, stem size 5, ceramic-on-ceramic bearing)

Procedure: positioned on the left side. Watson-Jones (anterolateral) approach. Layer-by-layer dissection. Femoral neck resected with an oscillating saw. Acetabulum reamed, cementless press-fit cup. Stem size 5 inserted, stable fixation. Ceramic head fitted. Reduction: easy, good stability in all directions. Thorough irrigation, bleeding controlled. Drain placed (Redon 12 Ch). Wound closed in layers.

Blood loss: about 280 ml. No transfusion.
Drain output first hour: 40 ml.

Post-operative orders:
- Mobilisation from day 1 with physiotherapy, full weight bearing allowed
- Post-operative X-ray of the right hip
- Continue heparin 5,000 IU subcutaneously
- Restart ramipril tomorrow morning
- Metamizole 1 g IV as needed, alternatively paracetamol 1 g IV

Complications: none during surgery.

P001-D016.title: ICU transfer report
P001-D016.text:
Transfer report, 07.09.2024, 12:00
Patient: Bruckner Hermine, born 17.04.1952, P001

Reason for transfer: post-operative pneumonia with respiratory decompensation and new atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

Admitted to ICU (bed ICU-3).

Status at transfer:
Temp 39.1°C, BP 138/90, pulse 118/min (AF), SpO2 91% on 4 l O2.
Blood gas: pH 7.41, pO2 66 mmHg, pCO2 37 mmHg, lactate 1.4 mmol/l.

Lab (taken 07:00):
  Hb 9.2 g/dl, leucocytes 16.4 G/l ↑↑, CRP 164 mg/l ↑↑
  PCT 2.1 ng/ml ↑ → infection likely
  Troponin T hs: 42 ng/l [ref: <14] ↑ → possibly due to AF
  BNP: 380 pg/ml ↑
  Creatinine: 1.05 mg/dl

ECG: atrial fibrillation, HR 115/min, no ST elevation.

Treatment started:
- Antibiotic: ampicillin/sulbactam 3 g IV every 8 h (start 11:30)
- Rate control: metoprolol 5 mg IV slowly, then metoprolol 47.5 mg orally 1-0-0
- Anticoagulation: heparin IV infusion (initially 1,000 IU/h, adjusted by aPTT)
- Oxygen: 6 l/min by mask → SpO2 95%
- Fluids: NaCl 0.9% 500 ml IV over 4 h
- Ramipril paused for now (BP borderline)

Clinical question for ICU: could the pneumonia mimic a pulmonary embolism? CT chest with angiography once stable.

2. New atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (I48.0)

Report: CT chest with contrast angiography, 08.09.2024
Patient: Bruckner Hermine, born 17.04.1952

Clinical question: pulmonary embolism? (shortness of breath and atrial fibrillation)

Findings:
Pulmonary arteries: normal contrast filling centrally and segmentally on both sides. No filling defect suggesting pulmonary embolism.
Lungs: consolidation in the right lower lobe, consistent with lobar pneumonia. Slight pleural reaction on the right. No pneumothorax.
Heart: no pericardial effusion. Heart rate due to AF. No pulmonary venous congestion.
Mediastinum: normal.

2. Lobar pneumonia of the right lower lobe, with pleural reaction.

P001-D019.title: Cardiology consultation – atrial fibrillation
P001-D019.text:
Cardiology consultation report, 09.09.2024
Consultant: Senior Dr Heinrich Fabian, cardiology
Requested by: intensive care

Reason: new atrial fibrillation (since 07.09.2024), persistent.

History: Mrs Bruckner, 72 years, known arterial hypertension, after surgery (total hip replacement 04.09.2024). No known AF. Right pneumonia (on ampicillin/sulbactam).

Echocardiography (09.09.2024):
- LV: EF about 55%, no regional wall motion abnormality.
- LA: slightly dilated (44 mm).
- Valves: no relevant stenosis or regurgitation.
- No pericardial effusion.
- No thrombus in the left atrial appendage (no TEE, TTE window adequate).

ECG: AF, HR 94/min, no sign of ischaemia.

AF risk assessment:
- CHA₂DS₂-VASc score: 4 points (hypertension 1, age ≥75: 2, female: 1) → anticoagulation clearly indicated.

Recommendation:
1. Rate control: continue metoprolol 47.5 mg 1-0-0 (target HR <90/min at rest).
2. Anticoagulation: switch from IV heparin to apixaban (Eliquis) 5 mg twice daily once kidney values are stable. Start apixaban when creatinine is stable and ICU discharge is near.
3. Rhythm control: no cardioversion for now (pneumonia, haemodynamically stable). After the pneumonia has healed, echo check and possibly elective cardioversion in 4–6 weeks.
4. Check thyroid values (TSH) for a thyroid cause of AF.

Diagnosis: first diagnosis of atrial fibrillation (I48.0), probably triggered by surgery/inflammation.

P001-D026.title: Cardiology follow-up consult – persistent AF
P001-D026.text:
Cardiology consultation report, 15.11.2024
Consultant: Senior Dr Fabian

Reason: AF follow-up. Patient still on ward UC-2 (long stay after hip replacement and complications).

Findings:
Patient well. AF persistent, rate 72/min. No heart failure symptoms.
Echo (today): EF 58%, LA 44 mm, no thrombus seen.

Rhythm control: pneumonia healed for >8 weeks. Cardioversion now possible.
Recommendation: elective external cardioversion planned for 20.11.2024 if the patient consents. Apixaban must have been taken for ≥3 weeks before cardioversion (since 11.09., so >2 months → OK).

Now: keep apixaban 5 mg twice daily. After cardioversion: continue apixaban for at least 4 weeks, then reassess CHA2DS2-VASc.

Thromboembolism prevention: continue apixaban, score 4 → long-term recommended.

P001-D027.title: Electrical cardioversion – sinus rhythm restored
P001-D027.text:
20.11.2024, 10:00, Senior Dr Fabian / cardiology

Elective external cardioversion under sedation (midazolam 2 mg and propofol 50 mg IV).
Biphasic shock 150 J → sinus rhythm restored.
ECG afterwards: sinus rhythm 64/min, narrow QRS, no sign of ischaemia.

Monitoring for 4 h: sinus rhythm stable, no complications.

Medication:
- Continue apixaban 5 mg 2-0-2 (at least 4 weeks after cardioversion, then outpatient cardiology)
- Continue metoprolol 47.5 mg 1-0-0 (prevent recurrence, blood pressure)
- Continue ramipril 5 mg

Plan: discharge end of November, outpatient cardiology check in 4 weeks.

P001-D028.title: Discharge letter after long stay
P001-D028.text:
Discharge letter
Musterstadt Regional Hospital, Department of Trauma Surgery
Date: 28.11.2024

Dear Dr Strohmayr,

We are discharging Mrs Hermine Bruckner, born 17.04.1952, after an inpatient stay from 02.09.2024 to 28.11.2024 (87 days).

Main diagnoses:
1. Medial femoral neck fracture, right (S72.00) – treated surgically
2. Status after cementless total hip replacement, right (04.09.2024)
3. Post-operative right-sided pneumonia (J18.1) – healed
4. First diagnosis of atrial fibrillation (I48.0) – sinus rhythm after cardioversion (20.11.2024)
5. Arterial hypertension (I10)

Secondary diagnoses:
6. Post-operative anaemia (D64.9) – improved

Course:
Admitted on 02.09.2024 after a fall at home. Right total hip replacement on 04.09.2024 without complications. On day 3 after surgery fever and shortness of breath → pneumonia and new AF. ICU stay 07.09.–13.09.2024. CT angiography on 08.09.2024 showed no pulmonary embolism. Antibiotics: IV ampicillin/sulbactam, then oral amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, 10 days in total. AF: rate control with metoprolol, anticoagulation with apixaban. Cardioversion on 20.11.2024 – sinus rhythm restored.

Medication at discharge:
1. Ramipril 5 mg (Delix) 1-0-0 – hypertension (unchanged)
